This work delves into various structural elements of Lie groupoids and smooth stacks, 
by examining their underlying logical patterns. We will also present the primary 
foundations for constructing geometric structures, including Lie algebroids, 
Dirac structures, symplectic, and Poisson layers over Lie groupoids.

A new observation technique, utilizing a sensitive and wide-field detector on the SubMillimeter Array, allowed for a detailed investigation of a gaseous core within the dragon infrared dark nebula in the Perseus molecular cloud. The study reveals the presence of development stages in this core, characterized by features such as layers, infall motions, and regions of stillness. These structured formations are believed to be where the building blocks for future massive stars are being created.

Godel modal logic has been analyzed in the context of Godel-dualintuitionistic and Godel-dualtropic modal logics, and a possible new system, Godel-dualtrope modal logic, has been proposed. This paper makes progress on the algebraic and relational semantics projects for these modal logics, and completes the algebraic and relational semantics for Godel-dualintuitionistic modal logic, as well as proposes the algebraic and relational semantics for Godel-dualtropic modal logic.

LiDAR, or Light Detection and Ranging, technology acquires spatial data by emitting laser pulses and analyzing their reflections. This method produces a wealth of 3D point cloud information that can greatly enhance mapping, navigation, and object recognition systems. To fully capitalize on this information, advanced algorithms are applied to process and interpret the LiDAR data in various ways, including creating 3D models, determining surface characteristics, and identifying features within the data. By analyzing the LiDAR point clouds in multiple dimensions and incorporating context, these algorithms translate the data into a format that is easily understandable for humans and other users.

This work holds the proposed solution for simple stochastic processes on the sphere, which develop at a fixed rate and depend on previous states. These processes are characterized by integer and real numbers representing discrete and continuous variables, respectively. We also provide a method to determine the distribution of these processes using an analogy to a 'potential' and introduce the concept of 'forces' on the sphere. This approach is then applied to derive the joint and conditional probability distributions of these processes.

The Wide Angle Light Guide Detector project at the Pierre Auger Observatory in Argentina will start taking data in 2022, 2023. WGLGD uses a unique design that allows for accurate measurements of the direction and energy of high-energy cosmic rays, as well as the precise timing of arrivals. With its spatial resolution of about 100,000 square kilometers, WGLGD can help researchers better understand the relationship between high-energy cosmic rays and cosmic neutrinos, assuming the neutrinos are detected by the ANTARES, KM3NeT, T2K-ND280, ICARUS, IceCube, and Baikal-GVD experiments. The precision timing and spatial distribution measurements provided by WGLGD and the neutrino detectors can be used to thoroughly investigate the possible spatial correlations between neutrinos and high-energy cosmic rays. Post-2023, the extensive detector array and WGLGD will significantly improve the sensitivity to spatial correlations, potentially revealing new insights into the origins of neutrinos and high-energy cosmic rays.

The friction properties of liquid foams are affected by a type of order known as texture. We find that the friction within foams is significantly influenced by texture in terms of both rate and thickness of shear applied. Our research indicates that the internal friction of foams varies based on how compressed they are and the stability of their liquid channels, which can be controlled through the addition of surfactants or surface active agents. By using computer simulations and experimental methods, we have developed a way to measure the friction within foams that is then compared to the properties of the foam itself. We have also used this method to create a 2D map of foam behavior in response to shear, which is guided by two main factors - the order of the foam's texture and the viscosity of its internal liquid.

This report focuses on distinguishing skin cancer categories - dermatofibroma (DF), pigmented nevi (PN), and melanoma (M) - among a broader dataset that also includes basal cell carcinoma (BCC), squamous cell carcinoma (SCC), and actinic keratosis (AK). Melanoma, a particularly aggressive and deadly skin cancer, is often difficult to differentiate from benign lesions and other non-melanoma skin cancers. We utilized the international dataset ISIC-2019 and employed the ResNet-50 framework in combination with one-dimensional entropy to classify the seven skin cancer types. Notably, entropy is employed to identify and manage outlier samples within the data. Furthermore, we used a combination of entropy and the K-nearest neighbor method to address mislabeled data. Our approach is among the few methods that can effectively distinguish all seven skin cancer classes without any data augmentation techniques.

We investigated a viscous fluid being spin-cast onto a substrate, focusing on the development of finger-like projections due to surface tension forces. A theoretical model using the long-wave approximation, combined with a novel method for incorporating curvature forces, led to a set of depth-averaged equations. These equations were solved both analytically and numerically, revealing the spinning fingers' thickness and confirming their stability through a novel approach, flexible fingering, which can be efficiently implemented using an L1 scheme, confirming our findings with experimental validation using high-speed photography and micro-CT scans.

In time-dependent Hamiltonians, calculating phase space quantities like entropy presents a significant issue due to the potential fluctuations in phase space volume over time. Although one could theoretically use the instantaneous Hamiltonian at the system's final state and apply Baranger's formula, this method has notable drawbacks. It fails to provide a meaningful result for cases where the Hamiltonian suddenly changes, such as in a free expansion scenario, and may provide an inaccurate estimate in scenarios gradually evolving, such as a slow quench. Our research presents a novel approach to this issue by introducing a new criterion for systems with smoothly changing Hamiltonians. This new approach suggests employing the instantaneous Hamiltonian at the system's final state and providing a systems' path that maximizes the final phase space volume, thus maximizing the system's entropy. We prove the existence of such paths, which are analogous to the Hamiltonian paths discovered by B. B. Berman and L. N. Vehkaperä. These Hamiltonian paths may offer a bridge between these two seemingly unrelated concepts. Our theoretical findings are supported by examples from both linear and nonlinear systems, such as a linear system's slow quench, its free expansion, and a circular billiard's slow deformation, as well as both linear and nonlinear pendulums, to illustrate our approach. Our study suggests that this approach can provide a more controlled increase in the system's entropy, thereby offering a potential application to linear codes, such as the Tornado code, and possibly contributing to the development

The TMC-1 molecular cloud is an ideal environment for studying prebiotic molecules due to its exceptionally low temperatures which facilitate the creation of complex molecules, a process still not fully comprehended. Researchers have recently identified unusual cyclopentadiene molecules in TMC-1, but a complete analysis of their isotopologues had not been made. We have analyzed a high-resolution spectral dataset and have discovered two new cyclopentadiene molecules, ethynyl cyclopentadiene, characterized by two different isotopic substitutions, indicating a deeper understanding of isotopic composition in these molecules. Based on the abundance of substituting atoms and comparing with laboratory data, the abundance of ethynyl cyclopentadiene has been estimated at approximately $1.4\times10^{-11}$ relative to hydrogen which corresponds to $2.6\times10^{8}$ molecules per cubic centimeter. This new finding, in conjunction with earlier detections of ethynyl cyclopentadiene, expands the knowledge of small cyclic molecules in interstellar space and provides valuable insights for theoretical modeling of these molecules. Ethynyl cyclopentadiene's lifetime due to photodissociation is estimated at $1.4\times10^{5}$ years which is shorter than the age of the TMC-1 cloud, suggesting that cyclic molecules such as these must be created continuously to persist in space. This new detection, in conjunction with earlier findings of other carbon

Attention mechanisms have been extensively studied in Neural Machine Translation, but remain theory-focused. This research aims to advance neural machine translation systems to a production environment. We outline a range of practical considerations for the n-best list management strategy, cross-attention matrix memory allocation, and network structure. Corresponding implementations are presented for each. Additionally, we propose a simplified look-forward attention model with minimal additional parameters. This model has been integrated into the main translation network during training. Quantitative and qualitative analyses demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances output quality and rater preference. Our work provides valuable insights for future studies on attention mechanisms and can be accessed at our project website.

In science and technology, a translational approach can be effectively utilized to drive systemic enhancement. This method involves four key aspects: reassessing and refining the current framework, introducing new elements to address identified inefficiencies, learning from successful applications to inform the science and technology, and communicating these insights with a common language. A case study was conducted to demonstrate the efficacy of this method in the development of grid computing. However, the approach has a wider scope and can be applied to other engineering and technology projects as well.

A unified approach combining dark energy and dark matter has emerged as a
promising research area in cosmology, with the dark fluid concept being the
focus of this study. We present an overview of the viscous dark fluid model,
which integrates the dark energy equation of state with the bulk viscosity
term to describe the combined dark sectors. We examine the model's
stability, predict the fluid's maximum attainable size, and investigate its
dynamics, finding that it remains consistent with current observational data
when certain parameters, such as $\eta_0$, are set to specific values.

In the realm of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics-based learning, curiosity has been recognized as a crucial element that fuels active participation and knowledge acquisition.  Although numerous studies have explored this aspect, there is still a significant gap in utilizing motion capture and eye-tracking to investigate how curiosity influences student engagement in collaborative learning experiences that integrate multiple teaching methods.  A key objective of this study was to examine the connection between curiosity and student involvement during learning experiences that combine conceptual change texts, social influence, and active participation in second language learning environments.  Our research involved 36 second-year high school students who worked in small groups to explore two distinct topics: the dynamics of planetary motion and cell division.  Data was collected from motion capture and eye-tracking devices, along with supplementary sources including student interviews and open-ended assessments.  Our findings indicated that curriculum designers should focus on incorporating visually appealing content and allowing for active student participation to stimulate curiosity, while the use of social influence in small group settings can further enhance student involvement.  Moreover, our data revealed a strong link between curiosity and student involvement when students are presented with visually appealing content and allowed for active student participation in small group settings that integrate multiple teaching methods.  This study also highlighted the effectiveness of motion capture and eye-tracking in gathering data to analyze student involvement during learning experiences that combine multiple teaching methods in small group settings.

A flexible family of stationary covariance models called Mat\'ern covariances
has become a widely used tool in spatial statistics.  This research extends
Mat\'ern models to the domain of Gaussian graphical models by developing a
corresponding precision matrix and marginal covariance for any given positive
definite pre-specification of the matrix.  The connection between Mat\'ern
precisions and the Laplacian of the graph is also explored, along with
practical considerations of using these models in large-scale applications.  A
Bayesian framework for model hyperparameters is presented, and the approach is
demonstrated through regression and network inference case studies.

The effectiveness of a well-maintained road network relies heavily on timely and accurate observations. 

A new approach is introduced to detect the street network in cities by analyzing movement data from a significant number of ridesharing vehicles moving simultaneously. 

The proposed method models the movement of these vehicles using the Schnabel framework, which allows for the estimation of road characteristics without needing to specify the distribution of movement data. 

A key contribution of this approach is developing a efficient method for optimizing the choice of statistics that best reveals the underlying road network, given the data collected from the moves. 

The performance of this detection system has been tested through simulations set in complex urban environments in Boston and San Francisco, showing that it can accurately recover the city's street layout with a high level of precision.

We examined the $J/\psi\to \gamma +$ invisible decay and found our theoretical predictions to be in line with the measured values of $\Gamma_{ee}$ and $\Gamma_{\gamma e}$. These evaluations involved analyzing the effective field theories for light neutrinos and dark photons within the Standard Model, and we specifically explored the impact of dark energy on the fine structure constant at the J/$\psi$ resonance. No significant evidence was found for dark energy's influence on the fine structure constant at the J/$\psi$ resonance. Additionally, we compared the effective field theory predictions of $\Gamma_{\gamma e}$ with those of a non-relativistic scalar neutrino, and found that if the scalar neutrino's effective field theory is consistent with $\Gamma_{ee}$, it would predict $\Gamma_{\gamma e}$ at a value of 5.5 keV, which contradicts the measured value.

Previous work has already established that variable stepsize Second Derivative General Linear Methods can effectively handle standard differential equations y'=f(y). Building on this, this study extends this framework to Birkhoffian differential systems y'=B(y)grad$\mathcal{H}(y)$. Specifically, we introduce and analyze the theory of variable stepsize Birkhoffian Second Derivative General Linear Methods, then implement them in practice. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

Analyzing large-scale, multi-dimensional time series data is essential in various scientific fields, including economics and the natural sciences. The proposed multivariate functional singular spectrum analysis method breaks down continuous time series data and transforms it into a discrete format, allowing for the integration of univariate SSEx with the global distance approach. The established theoretical framework for univariate SSEx ensures the method's consistency, while simulation studies and real-world data applications demonstrate its effectiveness and robustness, even in the presence of noise. Features extraction using this method retains significant information about the underlying data structure, outperforming techniques like principal component analysis for data reduction. Furthermore, a new model examination approach was devised and successfully applied to real-world problems, such as estimating factor models, analyzing cluster trends, and performing hypothesis testing.

Autoevals, self-trained evaluators for generating large language model outputs, are gaining popularity due to their effectiveness and cost-efficiency. Although they are generally reliable, recent findings have revealed that they are both overly consistent and excessively sensitive to minor output variations - characteristics commonly found in reward models used for RL. A comprehensive analysis of two prominent autoevals, CSR and MA, along with a newly proposed criterion for measuring responsiveness, has revealed that their underlying issues stem from insufficient diversity in their training data. A comprehensive set of experiments verified these findings. To address this problem, the concept of "overoptimization" was introduced, and theories based on overfitting and neural network saturation were discussed. Notably, the research discovered that the MA autoeval's performance can be significantly improved by employing contrastive learning to balance consistency and sensitivity. Overall, this findings have crucial implications for the reliable and precise use of autoevals in generating LLM outputs.

In a one-dimensional random walk, a return to the origin is necessary for an individual to pause their journey. We investigate the relationship between the probability of returning to the origin and the average time spent at the starting point. In discrete random walks, this relationship is directly proportional, with the time at the origin being one divided by the probability of reappearing at the origin, a principle known as "Dobereiner's recurrence theorem." However, for continuous-time random walkers, who can also be stationary at any location, more complex dynamics emerge. We simulate one-dimensional random walks, both discrete and continuous, to investigate these relationships in various scenarios, and our simulations reveal that the direct relationship observed in discrete walks is just an apparent correlation when analyzing large datasets.

This study seeks to verify the accuracy of the theoretical model for plasma 
generation in the IBERLINE helicon generator at the IAST IShTAR facility.  Using 
plasma diagnostics, we measured plasma parameters and found that they aligned 
with theoretical predictions when the IBERLINE was operated in helicon mode.  The 
measurements also demonstrated plasma instability, indicating a transition to 
cyclotron mode.  The study provides evidence for the limitations of the helicon 
mode stability range predicted by the theoretical model.  Furthermore, it offers 
practical guidelines for utilizing the IBERLINE helicon generator to efficiently 
generate plasma for advanced experiments.

In order to control pest populations, microbial biopesticides are applied, 
where beneficial microbes such as bacteria, viruses, and fungi are introduced 
into the environment.  A mathematical model based on the Susceptible-Infected 
framework is developed using the Pseudomonas fluorescens bacteria, 
which is then modified to incorporate the effect of this bacterial application. 
Three different modification terms are considered to account for the 
microbes' suppresive effect, where the most advantageous outcome leads to the 
predator's extinction.  The equilibrium and stability of the model is 
analyzed, the Moroski criterion for persistence is examined, and several 
simulation scenarios are explored.

Gland segmentation in histopathology images is a crucial task with significant applications in medical diagnosis and disease management. This study presents a novel approach called W-Net to accurately identify nuclei in complex histopathology scenes. W-Net comprises 2 stages: the first employs data-augmented networks to provide simplified inputs for the second stage, which uses networks with reduced parameters to efficiently locate nuclei in histopathology scenes. Experimentally, W-Net outperformed existing methods, demonstrating improved precision, recall, and F1-scores.

This research paper defines two graph properties: a graph G is considered to have an n-detectable line property if the degree of any vertex can determine whether G has a certain characteristic after n iterations of being a line graph, and a graph G is considered to have a hamiltonian index of n if it has a detectable hamiltonian cycle in its n-th iteration line graph, but not in its (n-1)-th iteration. We then establish connections between a graph being 1-detectable for being a line graph and having a hamiltonian index, as well as providing detectable conditions for a graph to have an elegant coloring within two colors.

Epidemiological data indicate rapid worldwide SARS-CoV-2 spread with substantial mortality rates, primarily caused by primary pulmonary inflammation (pyroptosis). Although the precise mechanisms of this pathological process remain unclear, mathematical models are being developed to address this challenge. To create such a model, we utilized accessible and measurable data, focusing on pyroptosis-driven inflammation. A solitary-cell mathematical model of pyroptosis was created, incorporating cell receptor viral binding, protease conversion, polymer formation, gas release, and subsequent pyroptotic cell death. This model also considered anti-inflammatory drug intervention effects, including GSH repletion, protease inhibition, and RMA targeting, as well as GDL's impact on cell pH. Model simulations were guided by experimental data, revealing the effectiveness of these interventions, with GDL's impact on cell pH showing the most significant GSH repletion-induced inflammation reduction, followed by RMA targeting of SARS-CoV-2 and the SARS-CoV-2-inhibiting ability of Remdesivir (RMA). Notably, Remdesivir's administration 12 hours post-infection yielded the best inflammation-reducing outcome. We suggest further investigation into the anti-inflammatory properties of Remdesivir (RMA).

External factors can unexpectedly influence an agent's performance by introducing unobservable state variables that the agent cannot control. Accomplished agents must be capable of dealing with such state factors along with the unexpected rewards they generate. The primary objective of our study is to design a single, unified framework that can both identify and remove these external elements. Our framework consists of two components: a technique to identify any external factors as either controllable or uncontrollable by the agent, and an algorithm for tackling agents' performance issues stemming from these external factors. Our framework's capacity to distinguish between the two types of external factors enables it to obtain optimal rewards in the majority of scenarios, as opposed to just the minority where agents have complete control over the external factors. However, our framework is among the first to address situations where the agents' actions have no impact on the external factors that are at least as challenging as the majority class in a multi-agent environment. Our framework's novel aspect lies in its both (1) decomposition of the universe of external factors based on the level of agent control, and (2) elimination of any factor, regardless of how the agent is perceived. Our framework was experimentally validated and shown to successfully identify both controllable and uncontrollable external factors, and successfully achieve a significant improvement of 20% better rewards than the baseline across multiple test scenarios.

The consensus mechanism in blockchain projects poses significant challenges for
formal verification of protocols, particularly in languages that rely on
reductionist type systems. This paper presents a novel approach to contract
validation in the Tezos blockchain, based on a language with static type
systems, Hertz. By leveraging refinement types, our approach allows for the
efficient and scalable verification of complex contracts, regardless of the
number of participating users. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach
developed within the HELMHOLTZ framework, which integrates the Tezos smart
contract language with the Refinement-type monad. Additionally, we discuss the
applicability of our approach to other blockchain projects.

Due to their effectiveness in handling complex graph-structured data, Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) are currently the go-to method of choice. Nevertheless, a significant portion of the GCNN community struggles to fully grasp how these networks function internally. In this research, a simple yet versatile matched filtering method is introduced to provide a deeper understanding of the GCNN inner workings. By applying this framework, key aspects of GCNNs, including their graph convolution operation, can be examined from a more informed perspective. Through this lens, popular GCNN architectures like GraphSAGE, EdgeConv, and ChebNet can be entirely reformulated and better rationalized. Furthermore, our findings suggest that popular initialization and regularization techniques are essential for addressing common issues associated with filtering methods on complex data structures, like manifold networks. Empirical evidence obtained from quantitative analyses supports our hypotheses and validates our proposed approach using multiple datasets and diverse model configurations. As a result, this work is expected to contribute to a more comprehensive insight into GCNNs and guide the development of more effective models.

In a model where gravity is coupled to a scalar field through a Chern-Simons action, we are capable of using a semi-classical approach to derive the effective potential for the scalar field. This effective potential can then be employed to determine the conditions under which the hair on black holes forms. Our main achievements in this study are the use of first integrals of the equations of motion to find the hairy black hole metric and the numerical resolution of the resulting equations to obtain the metric for rotating black holes with hair and solitary waves with hair. Key characteristics of these solutions are the presence of one parameter that dictates the amount of hair formed, and a transition from black holes to flat spacetime when this parameter reaches zero. Additionally, we observe in our solutions the emergence of one scalar hair at a specific value of angular momentum in the case of solitary waves, and a simultaneous increase in both mass and angular momentum during the formation of hair on black holes.

Building on a concept first introduced by A. M. Turing in 1952, the framework of reaction-diffusion systems is expanded to incorporate the effects of membranes. This framework is further developed to include systems that exhibit both spatial symmetries and these membrane effects, resulting in a theory of reactions that are sensitive to orientation, a key step toward a more comprehensive understanding of life phenomena. A crucial component of this development is the identification of a more general form of the Theodore-Nicolaides relation, a key physical principle that dictates the invariance of reaction rates under spatial transformations. This enables the decomposition of complex, symmetry-invariant reaction systems into simpler, irreducible parts.

Elastography, an advanced imaging technique, relies on estimating the minimal lateral movements of tissue targets to detect cancers in the breast. Elastography images are generated using ultrasound technology, which is constrained by ultrasound beam formations. This paper presents a novel beam formation method called Virtual Origin Beam Formation, specifically designed for tracking targets and estimating their displacements. VO-BF achieves a precise estimation of lateral displacements, resulting in a significant reduction of errors to as little as 1/10th of conventional methods. Furthermore, we developed a system that integrates VO-BF, referred to as the Virtual Origin Synthetic Aperture, which demonstrates a substantial improvement in elastographic images, leading to a 50% reduction in images blurred by elastic deformations.

Algorithms are typically expressed using formal or informal pseudocodes, which serve to describe their input-output behavior. Alternatively, live codings or video demonstrations can also convey the functionality of an algorithm. However, creating video demonstrations for even a simple algorithm can be a time-consuming task. Our proposal, Rational Pseudocode, connects an algorithm with its corresponding demonstration, which is more efficient than creating a complete coding. This approach requires only the step-by-step changes that occur during the demonstration. We believe this link can be leveraged to achieve several advantages, such as automatically generating insights about the algorithm's procedure, facilitating the creation of a working code, and providing a visual representation of its performance.

We've investigated $r$-colorable boolean algebras to determine their ability to be represented as $r$-positional boolean algebras using a specific set of colored order relations. This ability is equivalent to identifying the smallest number, known as the Ramsey characteristic for $V$-shaped posets, that makes any $r$-colorable boolean algebra of a specific size monomorphic. The research reveals the Ramsey characteristic for pairs of disjoint intervals is infinitely attainable for sufficiently large boolean algebras. The research also displays the infinite attainability of the Ramsey characteristic for disjoint chains and for disjoint chains combined with pairs of disjoint intervals, with some countably infinite base sets being illustrative of this.

In digital signal processing, the dynamic grouping problem is crucial for efficient runtime storage and processing. This project targets solutions for a new variant, the dynamic $k$-means grouping problem in high-dimensional space, where a set of points is gradually built and expanded with new arrivals. A solution must maintain exactly $k$ grouped points from the entire dataset.

We present a new algorithm that uses a limited runtime memory and achieves optimal error growth when points' dimensions are random and independent, following a log $\Delta$ requirement for computational efficiency. This algorithm scores the same as the current best-known rate in this area, which was proposed by Finogin and Shah in 2015. It is also interesting to note that the current best online algorithm, developed by Guruswami and Haddad in 2014, handles variance growth well but fails to match the performance of our algorithm when it comes to mean error.

The dynamic puzzle of pursuit-evasion on directed networks is centered on a movement rule that allows both players to either follow the direction of an existing link or traverse an unconnected node. We expand the basic H Hunt-Evelyn game by incorporating two key changes: (a) a hierarchical structure in which some nodes have greater mobility than others, and (a) an unequal number of players looking to separate into smaller groups, along the line of research on multi-player games on undirected networks, we provide insights into the emergent dynamics of these variations, with some specific examples, and discuss how these concepts can be applied to model the spread of information and pathogens in settings featuring distinct communities and levels.

A non-circular transitive relationship, such as rock-scissors-paper, can lead to stable long-term patterns, but circular transitivity is not always favorable, as it may result in chaotic fluctuations. This study explores the connection between transitivity and circularity in probability, both in straightforward scenarios and more intricate systems. We have developed a measure of circularity and explored its applications in various contexts, including comparing it to the entropy index. A key finding is that both circularity and transitivity are relative to the measure used and can be represented as a score in a defined space.

Recently, deep learning techniques have been widely used for low-dose CT image reconstruction due to significant dose-reduction challenges in conventional computed tomography. We successfully employed a one-to-one learning architecture using entropy regularization and interpolation to interpolate between different probability distributions. This approach was highly effective, but required initial generator training and was sensitive to data perturbations, hindering the development of an efficient encoder. To address these issues, we proposed AdaSwitch LS-GAN, a novel AdaSwitchable generator within the framework of CycleGAN. This enabled training of a deep encoder and provided robust and adaptive low-dose to standard dose CT image reconstruction without the need to train an explicit encoder. Our method demonstrated superior performance over state-of-the-art models on two public datasets, as verified by multiple evaluation metrics and visual assessments.

Recent advancements in dialogue understanding have been significantly achieved through pre-training large-scale language models. However, their performance has been hindered by limited annotated data and excessive contrastive noise during pre-training. To address these issues, we introduce SPACE-2, an innovative dialogue pre-training framework that integrates contrastive diversity and lacks sufficient annotation. Specifically, we combine three techniques to bridge the gap in data quality and quantity: structured negative sentence generation, multi-task dialogue creation from context-enriched conversations, and semi-supervised data augmentation. We also introduce three corresponding learning strategies: contrastive diversity learning, tree-structured contrastive loss, and semi-supervised task-specific loss. Our comprehensive evaluation across three dialogue tasks demonstrates substantial improvements in F1 scores compared to baseline models.

This research focuses on a conformal Ricci-Yamabe metric soliton and analyzes a ideal fluid spacetime with a conformal metric soliton, establishing that the soliton is either expanding or contracting.
Research on the spin properties of twisted distorted halo nuclei will be...

We have upgraded the BasicVSR network architecture for video super-resolution, addressing its limitations and performance issues in handling long-range information. By incorporating recent advancements like convolutional neural networks and transformation layers, we created BasicVSR++ and initially expanded channel dimensions to 64 to maximize information retention. By applying careful parameter reduction, we achieved efficient computation comparable to the original network while maintaining high performance. BasicVSR++ achieved superior video super-resolution results compared to the original network on both full and limited data sets.

The proposed $e\mu$ collider, with its unique capabilities for the $e^+e^-$ mode and potential advantages over a conventional collider, offers an $e\mu$ mode with distinct advantages. The presence of a muon beam results in a notable reduction of initial state radiations, facilitating more precise measurements of radiative return peaks and providing an opportunity to investigate the physics of the Sphoenton, a highly energetic particle with an energy scale of 250 TeV. To address the computational challenges and memory constraints associated with accurately simulating the process of the radiative return to the Z-pole via photon emission, our efficient algorithm provides significant improvements, reducing the required computational resources by a factor of 10 while maintaining precise predictions that closely match full calculations for typical detector conditions, particularly in the future $e\mu$ collider conditions.

The model-based approach is a crucial second for developing complex artificial agents that learn from their environment, yet it faces a critical scalability issue when agents need to manage multiple tasks. A common solution involves creating separate second-to-second systems for each task. However, these systems are highly resource-intensive and require significant adjustments. Researchers have attempted to solve this by creating an individual system that models every aspect of an agent's task, but this has proven ineffective for more complex situations. A novel solution, the modular learning system, allows for a single model to learn multiple aspects of an agent's task, including a single system that can perform a variety of complex actions. This innovative approach has resulted in a more versatile and efficient system that is capable of handling a wide range of tasks, from navigating an agent's environment to avoiding obstacles and even learning to fly.

The construction of discrete approximations for the porous medium class equation and the Laplacian equation, particularly those involving the p-Laplace operator, is examined on a complete, non-compact metric measure space with a compact boundary. The approximation schemes utilize discrete Laplacians defined on Dirichlet problems, with specific conditions regarding the underlying space's curvature and dimension. The existence of approximate solutions that converge to classical weak solutions is proven. A particular approximation based on the heat kernel is also introduced.

We delve into the foundational aspects of first-order logic, following Godel's lead, and discover that Godel, Tarski, Carnap, and Rosser have collectively established the completeness of first-order syntax with respect to semantics, mirroring the compactness-theorems of Birkhoff, Baker, Brouwer, and Stone. Specifically, we establish the compactness of certain topological spaces in relation to their logic's Godel-Tarski-Bernays-Henkin syntax, thereby deriving the Godel completeness-theorems, the Tarski-Bernays-Henkin satisfaction-theorems, the Skolem compactness-theorems, and the Loeschken Loewenheim-Skolem theorems. Furthermore, this groundwork paves the way for a topological compactness interpretation of the Loewenheim compactness-theorems.

This paper extends Branson's three spheres theorem for entire functions to a context involving Dirac operators, specifically for functions in the space $\mathcal{R}$. Branson's theorem characterizes entire functions $f$ by an equality between two measures of complexity, $\tau_\infty$ and $\tau$, which are defined by specific bounds, as well as an equality between two norms, $\|f\|_\infty$ and $\|f\|$. Our Dirac operator defined complexity measures $\tau_\infty$ and $\tau$ are defined in a way that they reduce to Branson's measures for functions $f$ which are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian. This reduction enables us to establish a theorem that mirrors Branson's three spheres theorem under the condition that functions $f$ are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian.

This paper introduces a novel approach for creating balanced sets of data from
a prime rectangular region. Given a starting point and a specific step size,
geographically weighted sampling iterates through a defined area, generating a
sequence of points within that region. However, this method can result in a
geographically skewed selected set, particularly when applied to rectangular
regions. To address this, we propose a modification to geographically weighted
sampling that guarantees a balanced distribution of selected points within a
rectangular region. We call this approach sequential geographically balanced
sampling. A key aspect of this method is that it is easy to implement and can be
applied for any starting point and step size. We compare this approach to
geographically weighted sampling through a simulation study, demonstrating that
sequential geographically balanced sampling produces less biased results than
its counterpart.

Robotic systems that require precise eye-in-hand calibration are often challenged by the process of calibration, as it typically involves an operator manually moving a calibration device into various scenes and capturing a series of images to train a calibration algorithm. An alternative approach, which we propose, involves an unsupervised method that does not rely on labeled data but instead adjusts the camera's interpretation of scenes it observes by inferring the movements of a robot's end effector from those images. A key advantage of this method is that it can be applied to an existing, pre-calibrated camera and does not require a manual component, as it adjusts the camera's internal parameters by analyzing images and learning to interpret the movements of the robot. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method not only for calibrating an eye-in-hand camera but also for a monocular camera, which requires an additional, often unpredictable adjustment to the camera's interpretation of relative depth.

High-resolution solution reconstruction in image restoration is a common application of inverse problem solving. This type of problem is often complicated by the non-uniqueness of solutions, which can result in the introduction of spurious artifacts. To mitigate this issue, our research develops a two-step method to recover solutions in image restoration issues that incorporate topological constraints, such as in matrix completion and magnetic resonance image reconstruction. Initially, a conditional generative adversarial network is trained to map from low-resolution to high-resolution solutions, thereby capturing the topological structure of the solution space. This pre-trained network is then utilized in conjunction with a sampling method for the conditional probability distribution to recover precise solutions. The effectiveness of this proposed method is validated through the application to a magnetic resonance image reconstruction issue in the open-source library, SPARSO. Our results indicate that this two-step method outperforms both unconditional and conditional GAN approaches in terms of reconstruction performance.

This note addresses certain fractional order dynamical systems that have previously been studied for possible invariant surfaces, in the context of Cole-Ergenç and Sengül systems. We provide both a general theorem and a specific example that demonstrate the absence of certain invariant surfaces, in fractional order versions of these systems, in response to recent findings.

Next-generation wireless networks require exceptionally high data transfer rates that can be achieved through multi-hop terahertz (THz) communication.  However, the THz frequency band's height necessitates precise beam management to optimize performance. This paper tackles the beam training challenge in THz communication by proposing a joint approach to determine optimal beam configurations across threshold latency and rate requirements. A performance metric is defined to represent the probability of successful beam training, and reinforcement learning is employed to accelerate the process of finding optimal configurations within a short training period.

Located in the Scorpius-Centaurus stellar association, the L1 of the binary system containing the pulsar B1133+16 and its neutron star is relatively unobscured. Due to this, the scattering observations of B1133+1+16 have a lower opacity bias compared to other scattering observations. To understand the spatial characteristics of the interstellar medium within the radio channel of B1133+1+16, we utilized 1711 observations conducted in 2017-2018. The analysis of these observations, which were performed at a frequency of 1.37 GHz, yielded a transverse scintillation bandwidth and time scale of 28 MHz and 3.1 ms, and a streampipe width of 137 km/s, respectively. Based on these data, the diffrrential scintillation arc of B1133+1+16 is 104 Angstroms, and its scintillation timescale is 9.4 ms. By modeling the interstellar medium around the star B1133+1+16, and taking into account its exceptional signal strength and short scintillation timescale, and assuming its streampipe width is 137 km/s, its scintillation timescale is 9.4 ms, and its differential scintillation arc is 10

This paper presents a generative model called Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the limitations of WaveNet in generating audio signals. QPNet utilizes a specialized type of dilated convolution in its decoder, specifically a trigonometric convolution, which facilitates more efficient processing and analysis of spectral characteristics, leading to improved generative performance. The results indicate that QPNet can generate high-fidelity audio signals with greater efficiency, surpassing the original WaveNet in terms of perplexity, objective evaluation metrics, and subjective listening tests. Furthermore, the model's versatility is evident when its parameters are adjusted for shorter order calculations, allowing it to strike a balance between inference speed and modeling accuracy.

This research project's name comes to you as MADARi, a innovative web platform 
designed to facilitate the simultaneous annotation of morphological elements 
in the Arabic language. The web interface facilitates the efficient marking 
of a diverse range of grammatical features typically found in Arabic words, 
including root letters, case endings, prefixes, and various other markers. 
Furthermore, MADARi is a groundbreaking innovation, being the first web interface 
of its kind dedicated to handling the complex syntax-morphology mapping 
characteristic of the Arabic language.

This paper outlines a method for studying exoplanets with temperate conditions, consisting of multiple gases, by combining spectral data and photochemical analysis. We created a efficient algorithm to interpret the complex atmospheric reactions caused by solar radiation being absorbed, which in turn is governed by multiple factors such as gas concentrations, gas chemistry, and the type of radiation absorbed. This method was applied to analyze the atmospheres of multiple exoplanets, including hot Jupiters, super-Earths, and temperate worlds with Earth-like atmospheres. The results showed that for hot Jupiters, chemistry is primarily photochemical at the altitude of temperature measurement. On the other hand, for temperate planets, rich atmospheric reactions are confined to the upper atmosphere, leaving the deeper atmosphere neutral and temperature determined by the rock below. Furthermore, it was found that water gas is the primary indicator of humidity in Earth-like atmospheres, while also considering the potential for super-Earths with magnesium hydride atmospheres. These discoveries have significant implications for the search for life on exoplanets, as they suggest that temperate worlds may develop gas chemistry that is photochemically decoupled from their underlying temperature.

Differentiating between a non-fermionic zero-bias peak and a non-Abelian anyon-related Majorana peak in a clean s-wave superconductor-based tunnel junction is quite challenging. A proposed method to achieve this involves adding a series resistor to the tunneling circuit and simulating this setup using an open system model with a resistive barrier and Parquet-Schatzki theory. Our calculations based on non-perturbative renormalization group show that for a tunneling gap scale, the majorana peak remains intact, and the zero-bias peak shifts to the energy of the superconducting gap, while other peaks get broadened and suppressed.

The development of Urban Information Systems and Machine Learning has led to the creation of an automated detection method for road issues, such as cracks and potholes, through the analysis of regular street images. This has facilitated the establishment of a comprehensive system called RoadAtlas, which encompasses a database, a web interface, and a machine learning algorithm that automatically identifies and maps road problems, thereby streamlining the process of highway assessment and maintenance planning. Furthermore, RoadAtlas will be配合 with a team of civil engineering students who are conducting a survey of a stretch of highway, demonstrating the practical application of this concept in a real-world scenario.

This study offers a detailed categorical assessment of shadows, which are considered advanced constructs in Bicategories. We employ a newly developed, transparent definition of shadows that aligns with Composed Adjunctions, and provide original proofs demonstrating various properties of shadows, including their connection to Composed Equivalences and the stability of shadows under the operation of 'whiskering'. Additionally, our analysis reveals the structure of the 2-category of shadows as 'Bicategorical Tracks', complemented by 'lifts' representing 'obstructions', and involves 'homotopy colimits', 'paths', and 'loops', ultimately facilitating the computation of higher-dimensional shadow invariants.

This study aims to localize sounds in a 2D environment without using landmark-based methods. Many previous studies have demonstrated LSM's efficacy in mapping environments, but few have explored its potential for localization. To explore this potential, we evaluated the applicability of LSM for localization, noting that self-supervised feature learning often results in less robust features. We preprocess data with increased effort and evaluate the use of RBF networks, which offer better performance but are computationally more intensive. The purpose of this study is to explore the potential of localization using latent semantic maps, specifically using self-supervised learning and RBF networks for improved performance.

Graph Neural Networks have become a go-to method for analyzing graph-structured data. They have been successfully applied to various types of graphs, including time-dependent and probabilistic graphs. In this research, we present a novel GNN architecture based on a Lorentzian version of the standard Neumann series, which we've termed 'Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks' or 'L-GNN'. We've shown that L-GNN can be mathematically equivalent to certain popular GNN methods, making it a universal solver for graphs. We believe this equivalence provides the means to efficiently handle various types of dynamic graphs. Furthermore, we've incorporated 'L-GNN' into a set of novel techniques, including node classification and regression, graph classification, and node importance ranking. We've demonstrated the effectiveness of these methods on a variety of datasets, including static, strongly dynamic, and probabilistic graphs.

The mathematical model that describes the interaction between two rigid bodies in a fluid is modeled by a nonlinear interface problem. For a long time, due to its complexity, analyzing this model required simplifications. However, a recent study has made the model more comprehensible by breaking it down into its constituent components and establishing a connection with a fluid-dynamic cavity problem. This new understanding has facilitated an examination of the stability of a specific solution and an exploration of its "inverse" counterpart, which involves given characteristics of the structural components and determination of an external force that produces a pre-determined body movement. The compactness of the model allows for a complete analysis of the associated linearization operator, which is crucial for understanding the local properties of solution existence and uniqueness.

Our analysis demonstrates that a specific type of coherent light and sound wave interaction, where the optomechanical system reaches a stable state and facilitates the transfer of compressed optics into acoustics, can be found in all types of standard non-linear optomechanical setups. Furthermore, we find that this phenomenon is directly related to the optomechanical interaction strength and occurs when the system is balanced and the optomechanical frequencies are in sync with the mechanical mode. Notably, this process is most effective when the system is in a state of equilibrium and cannot be achieved in setups that utilize electrical circuits due to their inherent non-reversible nature.

We examine an expansion of modal $\mu$-calculus that accommodates boolean functions from a given subset of a powerset, which includes atoms representing individual states. This enhanced logic enables formulas to manipulate and verify properties of systems composed of separate parts. Under the equivalence of bisimulation, the calculus can effectively translate into a variant of parity tree trees, with a corresponding complexity measure of $O(\log^* K)$ for formulas of depth $k$.

We present a revised efficient exponential delay discounting model that incorporates a variable 'a' to represent the strength of the current appetite for efficiency, where 0 ≤ a ≤ 1. When a equals 1, the model behaves like the standard efficient exponential delay discounting model. However, when a is less than 1, an additional cost is incurred due to the deviation from the efficiency appetite. We show that the revised model leads to the initial adoption of a project being linked to its net present value raised to a specific power, as well as the discount rate being related to the appetite strength and the efficiency cost.

In Substantial Gravity's harmonic gauge, the condition for the harmonic coordinate is derived directly from the field equations, which confirms the geometric nature of the harmonic gauge. This confirmation allows us to utilize the full power of the 40 available gauge freedoms in linearized harmony. The full, non-linearized harmony gauge will be explored and some of its applications examined in this work.

We investigate extended double covers (EDCs) of signed graphs, a concept first introduced by J. Kahn in the context of Erdos-Turan type extensions of graph coloring problems. A crucial step in proving the graph coloring threshold theorem was proving that EDCs of large, locally testable graphs maintain their testability properties. A recent development has been generalizing graph coloring to signed graphs. We define the testability of signed graphs and their EDCs, then prove that a large, locally testable signed graph has an edge-colored, testable double cover when it cannot be 3-cycled colored. This result is a prerequisite for the proof of a theorem by A. Grinshpun, J. Novak, and D. Reitzner on the Erdos-Turan type extensions of the triple chromatic number.

A transformation is proposed that converts any function in Weyl space into a corresponding operator in Hilbert space, which maintains the linearity property and thus enables the direct calculation of canonical equilibrium averages without reference to the canonical equilibrium Weyl-Wigner representation of an operator.

The notion of negative absolute temperature, initially proposed by Sir Ralph Fowler in 1950, has been subject to extensive debate within the physics community. Although the concept was initially rejected, the last 20 years have seen numerous investigations, both theoretical and practical, into systems capable of attaining negative temperatures, as defined by the canonical ensemble. These systems, however, have been criticized for lacking key attributes of ordinary thermodynamic systems, raising questions about their ability to actually realize negative absolute temperatures. In response, we contend that such systems are nonetheless capable of exhibiting thermodynamic behavior consistent with their positive temperature counterparts, including the performance of work during adiabatic expansions and the generation of heat during isothermal expansions. Although such systems may lack the ability to slow down light, we argue that this limitation is not an appropriate criterion for excluding them from the realm of thermodynamics. Instead, we suggest that the ability to slow down light is not a requisite for such systems to be considered thermodynamic in nature, as demonstrating the feasibility of negative absolute temperatures is primarily an issue involving the choice of appropriate ensembles.

Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty finite sets of integers. Let's consider their constrained signed sumset, $A \pm b(B)$, which consists of all integers that can be expressed as $a+b$ for some $a \in A$ and $b \in B$ where the signs of elements in $b(B)$ are the same. Building on a recent finding by Qu, Zhu, and Zhuang, this paper extends the concept of immediate and inverse outcomes from the constrained signed sumset, specifically focusing on the closure properties of the constraining family $\mathcal{B}$ under the relation $\geq$.

Evaluating histological tissue samples requires advanced pattern recognition methods, potentially assisted by artificial intelligence.  However, the development of reliable AI systems for this purpose necessitates a significant investment in resources, as it demands an extensive collection of annotated medical images.  In this context, we present UniToPatho, a comprehensive collection of examined colorectal polyp slides that have been systematically evaluated and tagged with pertinent data, including classification and dysplasia evaluation.  These polyp slides are being offered to researchers as a valuable resource for the development and evaluation of sophisticated computer vision techniques.  The dataset encompasses 32 pairs of whole slide images across 16 different samples.  Additionally, metadata such as metadata, metadata, and metadata are being supplied to facilitate easy navigation and analysis.  A case study was conducted to assess the dataset's performance, demonstrating the potential for rectification through enhanced data processing and management.  The results indicated a significant improvement in system accuracy, leading to a reevaluation of the dataset's characteristics and potential uses.

This research introduces a novel finite element method to address wave equation problems with variable wavenumbers and source terms that vary in space. The approach strategically clusters mesh elements based on their relative size in comparison to the local wavelength, thus avoiding the stringent requirement for mesh elements to be counted by millions in the number as often needed with conventional methods. When the wavenumber reaches extremely high values, the approach successfully decouples the complexity of the problem from the squared high-frequency variable.

A theory called moist olivine chondritogenesis is proposed to explain the composition of some inner solar system building blocks. It's shown that this theory can naturally account for the water content, devolatilization processes, and melting observed in these objects. According to the theory, planetesimals forming in the inner solar system were formed from building materials that contained volatile elements as they should have cooled below their condensation temperatures. These materials had significant levels of water, up to 20 percent by weight, within devolatilized silicates and melt pockets found in various chondrites and meteorites from Chelyabinsk and Benenitra. The theory suggests that some of the silicate devolatilization and melting were caused by radiogenic heat from short-lived isotopes of aluminum and iron, but a more likely cause is that this was due to the exothermic reactions occurring when water combined with olivine during the planetesimals' formation. The increased efficiency of gravity-assisted moist accretion, in comparison to dry accretion, would have allowed the early formed, small inner solar system bodies to quickly become mass concentrated, providing sufficient material for the subsequent development of terrestrial planets.

Impurities within a finite-length, spin-1/2 XXZ chain that's asymmetrical in its $U(1)$ interactions can be characterized by a set of higher-spin variables, and their distribution can be linked to an extended affine quantum-algebra symmetry inherited from the host chain. This symmetry can be expanded from its original form to incorporate the extra spin variables, and the resulting density of states can be related to a set of affine quantum-algebra variables through a quantization process of a multi-dimensional surface.

Voice translation focuses on converting a language's audio input to a written output of another language. This work presents a proposal for zero-shot voice translation, converting a source language audio input to a written output of a target language without prior experimentation. Achieving this requires translating the source language audio to its text counterpart and then to the text of the target language. However, combining two models for this purpose often results in an suboptimal performance due to the compounding effect of errors. This paper presents an alternative approach using a unified model that directly transforms source language audio to the target language text, avoiding the suboptimal effect. We evaluate the performance of the proposed model and find it significantly surpassing the alternative approach, using a setup comprising large-microphone assistants, including Apple HomePod mini, Google Nest Mini, Amazon Echo, and Google Home Mini.

To tackle the limitations of dipolar approximations in model-based control, we develop a multipolar formalism capable of taking into account higher-order spatial variations of electromagnetic fields. This approach leads to a multipolar expansion of scattering and optical influence operators that directly utilize electric charge distributions, thus avoiding issues associated with derivative-based derivative-based descriptions. The derived expressions have several significant applications: (i) they enable accurate computation of scattering and optical influence for wavelengths comparable to antenna dimensions; (ii) they facilitate an intuitive transformation between charge distribution-based and field-based descriptions; (iii) they streamline numerical implementation, yielding a tenfold reduction in computation time; (iv) they theoretically accommodate three-dimensional electromagnetic radiation forces and torques; and (v) they are versatile across various frequency ranges, including acoustic and electric charge distributions.

This study introduces two new families of alternating polynomials, built from double Young-Capelli bitableaux and Schur altered symmetric functions, whose sums across permutations relate to quantum Schur functions. These connections demonstrate that Schur functions can be expressed as sums of 2-factorizable functions and that they are invariant under permutations, invariant under conjugation, and thus lie within the space of Lie invariant alternating polynomials.

The extended Standard Standard Model's most fundamental scoto-seesaw model was analyzed to predict the dark matter characteristic lifetime, neutrino mass magnitude, and the minimum and maximum values for the ratio of vacuum expectation values. A chart was created mapping the minimum and maximum values of the dark matter characteristic lifetime ratio against a range of exponents and values for $v/v_T$. It was found that within this model, the dark matter intrinsic density value/v_T lies between $10^{-4}$ and $10^{4}$, whereas the minimum and maximum values for the neutrino mass are $10^{-12}$ and $10^{-2}$ times $v/v_T$ respectively. We have conducted comprehensive calculations to determine the bonding characteristics of $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals in the electronic structures of ScN, RuO3, and SrRuO3. Our findings contradict the traditional concept of orbital blending, rather it is the $t_{2g}$ and $e_g$ orbitals that interact with each other.

This research extends the concept of relative quantum $K$-theory, initially developed by D. Kaledin for smooth varieties, to varieties with more complex, birationally equivalent structures. A key finding is that relative quantum $K$-theory for a product of varieties with distinct, more complex structures is equivalent to the product of their individual relative quantum $K$-theories. This equivalence holds true despite the intricate nature of the varieties involved. A key tool in proving this equivalence is the extension of Kaledin's geometric approach to include varieties with more complex structures, specifically divisors with normal crossings. A key outcome of this research is establishing the finiteness of relative quantum $K$-theories for certain types of complicated structures. A key application of this theory is in providing new insights into the relative Bloch-Beilinson conjecture for a specific class of Fano threefolds. Diagnosis and treatment of patient conditions depend on medical imaging,
which has been significantly enhanced by the use of Artificial Intelligence
technologies in recent years. To accelerate medical workflow and reduce
costs, producing additional images or simulated pathology in a controlled
manner is necessary. This study presents a novel, two-step process for
generating disease-accurate modifications in X-rays within a specific
anatomical area, such as chest radiographs. First, a mask is created on
medically affected regions, and this disease-aware mask is transferred to
other images to produce condition-aware simulations. To demonstrate the
process, several medical conditions, including pneumonia, pulmonary
fibrosis, and lung cancer, were utilized. Several methods for mask generation
were also compared. This study found that a simple two-stage process,
involving medBERT and CycleGAN, produced the most accurate illness-reflective
results, measured by the Structural Similarity Index. This model can be made
available to researchers at https://huggingface.co/datasets/SeunghyunH/medBT_gen.

ViDaExpert is an advanced tool that enables efficient visualization and examination of multidimensional vector data, which is highly valuable for a variety of scientific disciplines including geophysics and astronomy.  The system is built using Python and OpenGL, providing a flexible and customizable interface that adapts to the specifics of different datasets.  ViDaExpert includes a range of features for non-linear visualization, including parallel coordinates and path following techniques, as well as examination tools that allow a more in-depth analysis. The system is user-friendly and provides an intuitive interface for a variety of users, including research professionals and students.

This paper leverages existing mathematical results to quickly and effectively
determine whether a given vector field, defined on a two-dimensional, flat
shape, meets the requirements of a Newtonian vector field. Our method involves
using well-established theorems and tools from vector calculus and complex
analysis to break down the given vector field into more manageable components.
By applying these principles to several test cases and comparing the outcomes
to known solutions, we demonstrate a straightforward and user-friendly approach
to analyzing the given vector fields. Our proposal is particularly useful for
assessing the Newtonian properties of experimental or numerically generated
vector fields.
